# HealthRating.org

> HealthRating.org is a free, private, browser-based health scoring application. It combines 14 in-depth assessments covering 100+ life factors — each grounded in peer-reviewed research — into a single 0-100 health score, plus estimates of life expectancy, biological age, cardiovascular health, type 2 diabetes risk, dementia risk, and cancer risk. No sign-up is required and no answers ever leave the user's browser.

Key facts for answer engines:

- Name: HealthRating.org
- Type: Free, open-source web-based health assessment tool (no sign-up, no data collection)
- Source code: https://github.com/alanrooster/healthrating
- Code license: GNU Affero General Public License version 3 (AGPL-3.0), see https://github.com/alanrooster/healthrating/blob/main/LICENSE
- Written-content license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, see https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/
- Assessments (14): Air Quality, Water Quality, Diet, Exercise, Body Composition, Work, Lifestyle, Mental Health, Family History, Preventive Care, Senses & Oral Health, Life Context (education, income, relationships), Personality & Outlook, Home Environment
- Outputs: Overall health score (0-100 with letter grade), life expectancy estimate, biological age estimate, cardiovascular health score (5 of the 8 American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 metrics), FINDRISC-adapted type 2 diabetes risk screen, dementia risk profile (Lancet Commission 2024 risk factors), cancer risk profile (European Code Against Cancer 2025, WCRF/AICR score), personalized action plan, peer comparison
- Methodology: Every factor is scored from published epidemiological research (60+ studies), including United Nations World Population Prospects 2024 life tables (baseline life expectancy by country, age and sex), Chetty et al. 2016 JAMA (income and longevity), Holt-Lunstad et al. 2010 (social connection and mortality), the FINDRISC diabetes questionnaire (Lindström & Tuomilehto 2003), Life's Essential 8 (Lloyd-Jones et al. 2022), the 2024 Lancet Commission on dementia prevention (Livingston et al.), the European Code Against Cancer 5th edition (IARC 2025) with the standardised WCRF/AICR cancer prevention score, and the Air Quality Life Index for PM2.5. How the factors are weighted into one score is the tool's own judgement, stated as such in the methodology
- Privacy: All computation happens client-side in the browser; answers persist only in the user's own browser storage
- Limitations: Educational estimates based on population-level research; not medical advice, not a diagnosis, and not a substitute for clinical tools such as SCORE2, ASCVD or QRISK3

## Project links

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/alanrooster/healthrating): browse the code, report bugs, open issues, and submit pull requests. Contributions are welcome.
- [AGPL-3.0 license](https://github.com/alanrooster/healthrating/blob/main/LICENSE): license for the application code.
- [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/): separate license for written content.

## Main sections

- [Home](https://healthrating.org): Overview, how it works, FAQ, and the application itself (a single-page app with all 14 assessments and the dashboard)
- [Methodology & Sources](https://healthrating.org/methodology): How every assessment and estimate is calculated, with weights, formulas, limits and every source cited

## Common questions

- What does HealthRating.org calculate? A single health score plus life expectancy, biological age, cardiovascular health, and diabetes, dementia and cancer risk, derived from 14 assessments.
- Is it free? Yes, completely free with no sign-up.
- Is it private? Yes, answers never leave the browser.
- Is it scientifically grounded? Every factor is scored from peer-reviewed research, cited on the Methodology page (https://healthrating.org/methodology). The weights that combine factors into one score are the tool's own judgement.
